_readme: A zone map. Copy this into a repository you want to classify changes in,
as skeleton.json, and edit the three sections below.
In production a zone map does NOT live in the repo it governs — it is
loaded from outside via Skeleton.load_file(), so an agent working in a
checkout cannot widen its own permissions. The in-repo location is for
local use and CI, where you are the one running it.
_limits: Shape budget for one session. These are not hard stops — going over
costs points. Size alone never blocks a change; it only makes stacked
filename_similarity and dir_population are the anti-sprawl pair: they
catch foo_v2.py appearing beside foo.py, and directories quietly
growing past the point anyone reads them.
_red: Frozen surfaces. One hit is categorical — no size of diff merges here.
Give every rule a reason: the reason is quoted back to the agent, and it
is the only explanation it gets.

red.reason: the metric an agent is graded on is not a metric it may redefine
infrastructure takes effect through a deploy, so it waits for a human

_zones: Where agents may write. green_for lists the agent ids allowed in.
Every zone needs an oracle: a command that exits non-zero when the
change did not work. A zone declared without one refuses to load, by
design — granting merge rights with no acceptance check is the failure
Verify each oracle catches a deliberately broken input before you open
the zone. An oracle that cannot fail is not an oracle.
